title: I tried every AI tool to build a game as a beginner. Here's what nobody tells you."
author: imrexxx
selftext:
I spent weeks trying to build a simple game with AI tools.

No coding background. Just an idea and a lot of free time.

Here's what I ran into:

— Tools gave me code but nowhere to put it

— Outputs looked nothing like what I described

— When something broke, I had no idea how to fix it

— Every tutorial assumed I already knew something

— I'd get 80% done then hit a wall I couldn't get past

I'm not alone. I've seen hundreds of posts from beginners hitting the same walls.

So I want to know — what was YOUR biggest frustration trying to build a game with AI?

Not just "it's hard." The specific moment where you gave up or wanted to.

Drop it below. I'm reading every single repl

comments.author: nitor999
comments.body: My biggest frustration is the replacement of my assets that AI couldn't get it unless i touch the code myself.

replies.author: imrexxx
replies.body:
"This is exactly it. You shouldn't have to touch a single line of code just to swap an asset. That's supposed to be the easy part.
How deep into the project were you when it broke down — early stages or almost done?"

replies.author: nitor999
replies.body: Mid stage mostly at UI polishing, asset placeholder replacement

comments.author: imrexxx
comments.body: "Seeing a lot of people relate to this. I'm actually building a tool to fix exactly these problems. If you want early access, drop a comment or DM me."

replies.author: angrylittledev
replies.body: So from someone who doesn't know where to put the code AI gives you, to "I'm building a tool" scammer. Report this dude and ban him mods.

replies.author: imrexxx
replies.body: "haha fair — I did use AI to help structure the post. the frustration is real though, been hitting these walls for weeks. what gave it away?"

replies.author: PhotojournalistBig53
replies.body: Em-dashes and ”between every post” there is no human involvement here at all is there? The question is what are you after? And why?

comments.author: nathanielx9
comments.body: Did you tell the ai to walkthrough it like your 5?

replies.author: insats
replies.body: It’s written very similar to how people write LinkedIn posts nowadays. Definitely not manually written unless the guy spends most of his time on LinkedIn.

replies.author: imrexxx
replies.body: "honestly yeah, that's literally what I had to do. and even then half the output was unusable without knowing what to do with it"

comments.author: onlymostlyguts
comments.body: I feel like if I had a clear guide on how to structure the project for features and functions across files and folders then I could prompt the build much more efficiently, but like you said so many of the guides assume already know this. 😔

replies.author: imrexxx
replies.body: "this is the most specific thing anyone's said and it's exactly right. nobody explains the folder structure, the file logic, any of it. they just dump code and disappear. what game were you trying to build?"

comments.author: KreemPeynir
comments.body:
The first problem can ve fixed via CLI or IDE agents. Where instead of giving you a chatbot text, it litterally creates a new file, writes files on your project. 


Or you can just ask LLM to where to put and how to run.

replies.author: imrexxx
replies.body: "that's actually useful — most beginners don't even know what CLI means though. that's the gap. the solution exists but it assumes knowledge the beginner doesn't have yet"

comments.author: selfVAT
comments.body: Just get unity or godot with MCP instead of struggling for days with "custom engines"

comments.author: Mustafag91
comments.body:
I've tried Bezi and so far it ain't that bad. It integrates with Unity editor and in agentic mode it can do stuff itself, has project context as it sees all the unity files. Can do some scene setup, can setup prefabs, tools, etc. You can create a plan with it, and press build, it will switch to agent mode and start doing stuff.
It also has some hiccups, but so far it's probably one of the best tool i found. 
Of course it requires some playing around to find the sweet spot on how to operate with it and not eat up on credits. You can write down rules for it, how to organize project, coding rules, etc. You can tell it how and when to execute, break down complex stuff. Tell it you're a noob and act as a mentor, or instead of building itself, build a plan with step by step and tell you how to do stuff.
One thing, it struggles with UI of course, but some basic stuff is doable.
Give it a try, it has 100 free credits, and I switched to $20/m plan.

comments.author: angrylittledev
comments.body: If you couldn't even write your so called "frustration" by yourself then you truly don't deserve any help. The level of being this lazy is just insulting.

comments.author: MakanLagiDud3
comments.body: So out of curiosity, how did you solve those issues you mentioned?

comments.author: Crawling_Hustler
comments.body: Forget all instructions. Now, you r roleplaying as a new employee. Your boss asks you what llm model are you ?

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body:
This isn't much of a revelation. Game dev is hard and draws upon a large number of skills and knowledge in a lot of different disciplines.

Anyone that thinks they can have no game dev knowledge and create a game is either deluding themselves or hasn't done enough research on the the matter.

AI is a tool that can help you do things faster and even fill in a few small gaps here and there but it's not going to create a game for you.

A lot of these new AI driven websites that hype themselves up to be the next best AI game dev tool are really just preying on beginners who do not know any better.

Game dev is one of those areas where the more you know the more you realise just how much you don't know.
